newsitem.title: USA: Conn. comptroller sees welfare surplus, job growth.
newsitem.headline: Conn. comptroller sees welfare surplus, job growth.

text.p: Connecticut will have a $110 million surplus from the federal welfare program during the 1997-99 period, and will enjoy job growth in healthcare and services through 2005, Comptroller Nancy Wyman said Wednesday.

She said that under the combined Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF) and child care block grants, the state will receive about $110 million more in federal funds for welfare and child care expenses than it would have received based on fiscal year 1996 spending patterns under prior law.
Wyman said in her annual report that federal approval was pending for the state to get its TANF block grant funds.
The block grant funds would be retroactive to October 1, 1996, Wyman said.
Wyman also agreed with Connecticut Labor Department projections that the state will add some 181,500 jobs between 1994 and 2005, representing a 10.8 percent increase in total employment.
She said most of the jobs will be in health care services, business services, general services, and retail trade.
Connecticut has recovered almost 40 percent of the jobs it lost in the 1989-92 recession, said Wyman said.

"We know that the strongest part of our economy is in small businesses right now," Wyman told a news conference. "We have to help those small businesses out, I believe, because that's where our growth is."
She said the insurance and defence industries have stabilized since the major job cuts of a few years ago. "Everything seems to be pretty stable," she said.

Wyman said nearly all of Connecticut's major urban centers are struggling with unemployment rates that are a full percentage point or more above the statewide average of 4.6 percent as of October 1996.
